waived_providers.reason: Claude produced no result on prior 1800-second and 900-second attempts and again timed out on bounded 600-second Sonnet and 300-second Haiku passes. The owner prioritized completion over provider availability.

The repository owner authorized completion without Grok when Grok is unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Grok may still be attempted as a bounded supplemental reviewer, but its failure never blocks a valid Claude plus no-tools result.

provider_policy.review_rule: Codex may complete source-grounded fallback research after bounded Claude and Grok attempts fail. It requires a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remains reviewable-draft with a visible absence-of-external-review hold.

boundary_decision.rationale: The model owns the claim identity, request-side assertions, claim lines and claim-owned amendment lineage. Policy, coverage, occurrence, party, subject, evidence, handling, assessment, decision, reserve, settlement, payment, complaint, dispute, fraud, recovery, regulator, audit and records remain external masters.

decisions.rationale: The aggregate owns the identity-bearing request, substantive claimant assertions, lines, requested values and version lineage without absorbing external policy, loss, evidence, processing or outcome masters.
The policy or insurance context owns the promise and coverage terms. The candidate CONTAINS relation grants no cascade authority and is represented as a required external basis reference.

The claim and handling case have different identity and lifecycle authority. A claim may have multiple handlers, reopened cases or coordinated insurers, so the candidate edge cannot imply one-to-one containment.
Receipt of notice does not by itself establish a fully presented, complete, admissible, valid, covered or payable claim.

decisions.concept: Claim status and external process states
decisions.rationale: Claim-owned draft, presented, amended, withdrawn, closed, reopened and superseded states do not silently determine handling, coverage, liability, settlement, payment, dispute or regulator states.

decisions.concept: Claimant assertion, observed fact and authority position
decisions.rationale: An allegation, observation, expert opinion, insurer position, settlement and regulator or court decision retain different authors, evidence, times and authority.

decisions.concept: Claimed, estimated, assessed, allowed, offered, reserved, settled and paid values
decisions.rationale: Each value preserves amount, currency, unit, scope, line allocation, source, method, uncertainty, event time and authority and never overwrites another class.
Policy existence and claim presentation do not establish coverage, liability or causal nexus; reasoned positions and decisions remain externally mastered.

decisions.concept: Duplicate, related, parent-child and successor claims
decisions.rationale: One occurrence may generate multiple legitimate claims and one claim may involve several policies or jurisdictions, so similarity alone cannot authorize merge or deletion.

decisions.concept: Complaint, dispute, fraud, recovery and regulator case
decisions.rationale: These cases may arise from or affect a claim but have independent identity, authority, procedure and outcome lineage.
FHIR R5 financial resources are Trial Use and domain-specific, while ACORD schemas are licensed; neither transport defines the universal semantic identity of the claim.
Personal, health, financial, location, evidence, fraud and legal data remain deny-by-default and disclosure requires scoped authority, purpose, minimization and audit.

decisions.concept: Single-provider waiver and local no-tools audit
decisions.rationale: One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audited the frozen validated result and comparison without acquiring new facts, so assurance remains reviewable-draft.

deferred_research: Approve or reject the WM-ECO-003 and WM-ACT-045 candidate relations and define claim-to-policy, claim-to-handling-case, multi-insurer, reopening, split and merge cardinality.
Create independently validated life, health, disability, workers compensation, property, motor, liability, travel, cyber, marine, reinsurance, catastrophe and public-scheme profiles.
Benchmark claim identity matching, claim-line codes, evidence requirements, amount classes, coordination of benefits, duplicate detection, privacy, retention and cross-border handling.
Validate jurisdiction, policy class, claimant standing, limitation, coverage, liability, settlement, payment, appeal, complaint, fraud and regulator rules.
Pin exact external releases and licensing conditions and obtain independent insurance, claims, legal, privacy, security and records review before promotion beyond reviewable-draft assurance.
publication_holds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-ECO-036 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external result was admitted.

Boundary hold: the aggregate owns claim identity, request-side assertions, lines and amendment lineage while policy, loss, evidence, handling, decision, settlement, payment, dispute and records masters remain external.
Relation hold: WM-ECO-003 CONTAINS WM-ECO-036 and WM-ECO-036 COMPOSE WM-ACT-045 remain candidate relations without approved cardinality or cascade semantics.
Insurance-line hold: life, health, disability, workers compensation, property, motor, liability, travel, cyber, marine, reinsurance, catastrophe and public-scheme claims need separate validation.
Jurisdiction hold: claim formation, deadlines, evidence duties, limitation, coverage, liability, remedy, privacy, retention and redress depend on jurisdiction, policy and insurance line.
State hold: notification, presentation, completeness, validity, coverage, liability, decision, settlement, payment, closure and finality remain independent.
Value hold: claimed, estimated, assessed, allowed, offered, reserved, settled and paid values remain separately sourced, timed and currency-qualified.
Authority hold: claimant assertion, observed fact, expert opinion, insurer position, settlement and regulator or court decision do not prove one another.
Identity hold: duplicate, related, parent-child, successor, multi-policy and multi-insurer relations require explicit evidence and must preserve predecessors.
Privacy hold: personal, health, financial, location, evidence, fraud and legal data require purpose limitation, minimization, access controls and auditable disclosure.
Source-access hold: ACORD licensed artifacts were not accessed; only official public overview material was used, and no ACORD conformance is claimed.
Maturity hold: HL7 FHIR R5 Claim-family resources are Trial Use and health-specific, not a universal claim model.
Interoperability hold: every FHIR, ACORD, code-list, temporal, provenance, quality and policy projection needs exact release pins, conformance evidence and loss declarations.
Review hold: insurance, claims, actuarial, legal, privacy, security, records and independent external review are outstanding.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
